title: A central coord service holds the job queue of every clone, and each executor, workstation, server or CI, takes only the jobs placed on its own kind
goal: kbjob.py takes the global --url URL --key-file PATH of coord.py, with the same plain-http refusal and key file mode rule, for submit, follow, status, log and cancel, which reach the job table of a central coord serve through POST /v1/run; kbjob.py serve --kind workstation|server|ci --url URL --key-file PATH takes from the central queue only the queued jobs whose placement executor is its kind, a workstation executor only those whose host id is its own and whose operator is the operator of its key file; a job with no placement is placed on the workstation; each job runs in the clone whose integration remote url equals the one the job names (no such clone leaves the job queued with the reason) and every move is posted back to the central store, so a job placed on another kind, host or operator stays queued; the central store keeps states and events only, the output log stays with the executor and log JOB names the host that has it

run:
import sys,os,tempfile,subprocess,json
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); kd=os.path.join(d,"keys"); os.makedirs(os.path.join(kd,"corp"))
k1=os.path.join(kd,"corp","jan.kowalski"); k2=os.path.join(kd,"corp","anna.nowak")
for k,t in ((k1,"k1key-placeholder"),(k2,"k2key-placeholder")): open(k,"w").write(t); os.chmod(k,0o600)
sv=subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--store",os.path.join(d,"c.sqlite"),"serve","--bind","127.0.0.1:0","--keys",kd],stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,text=True); import atexit; atexit.register(sv.kill)
url=sv.stdout.readline().split("serving")[1].strip()
kb=lambda key,*x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--url",url,"--key-file",key,*x],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=300)
st=lambda j: json.loads(kb(k1,"status",j).stdout)
r=kb(k1,"submit","check","--name","backlog-check","--no-ensure"); assert r.returncode==0, r; j=json.loads(r.stdout)["job"]
assert st(j)["placement"]["executor"]=="workstation"
kb(k2,"serve","--kind","workstation","--once"); s1=st(j)["state"]
kb(k1,"serve","--kind","server","--data",os.path.join(d,"srv"),"--once"); s2=st(j)["state"]
kb(k1,"serve","--kind","workstation","--once"); s3=st(j)["state"]
sv.terminate(); assert s1=="queued" and s2=="queued" and s3 in ("succeeded","failed"), (s1,s2,s3)

import sys,os,tempfile,subprocess,json,platform
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); kd=os.path.join(d,"keys"); os.makedirs(os.path.join(kd,"corp"))
k1=os.path.join(kd,"corp","jan.kowalski"); open(k1,"w").write("k1key-placeholder"); os.chmod(k1,0o600)
sv=subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--store",os.path.join(d,"c.sqlite"),"serve","--bind","127.0.0.1:0","--keys",kd],stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,text=True); import atexit; atexit.register(sv.kill)
url=sv.stdout.readline().split("serving")[1].strip()
kb=lambda *x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--url",url,"--key-file",k1,*x],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=300)
co=lambda *x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--url",url,"--key-file",k1,*x],capture_output=True,text=True)
st=lambda j: json.loads(kb("status",j).stdout)
def edit(j,**m):
    g=json.loads(co("get","job/"+j).stdout); rec=json.loads(g["value"]); rec.update(m)
    assert co("put","job/"+j,"--value",json.dumps(rec),"--revision",str(g["revision"])).returncode==0
j=json.loads(kb("submit","check","--name","backlog-check","--no-ensure").stdout)["job"]
good=json.loads(json.loads(co("get","job/"+j).stdout)["value"])["remote"]
edit(j,remote="https://example.invalid/other.git")
kb("serve","--kind","workstation","--once"); s1=st(j)
assert s1["state"]=="queued" and any(e["fields"].get("step")=="no-clone" for e in s1["events"]), s1
edit(j,remote=good)
kb("serve","--kind","workstation","--once"); s2=st(j)
assert s2["state"] in ("succeeded","failed") and s2["log"] is None and s2["log_host"]==platform.node(), s2
assert kb("log",j).returncode==0
edit(j,log_host="build-host-1"); r=kb("log",j)
sv.terminate(); assert r.returncode==1 and "build-host-1" in r.stderr, r

gates.question: Does a central service only queue jobs for workstation executors, or does a central executor also run operations?
options: queue-only: the central coord holds job states and events, and every operation runs on the workstation that holds the clone
central executor for check and benchmark runs only: it keeps a clone of its own and a credential for it
central executor for every operation, landings included
gates.recommendation: queue-only: the central coord holds job states and events, and every operation runs on the workstation that holds the clone
gates.answer: Central executors, a server kbjob.py serve and GitLab CI jobs, may run every operation, landings and worker sessions included, wherever the group's OPA placement policy puts the job, as the identity it names (none, group bot or the operator's own token); without a decision every job runs on the workstation (EP-p4guu2ip)
gates.host_unchecked: The central service the answer names is what this sprint builds; its checks prove it on a loopback coord serve with planted key files, and no deployed host exists yet to check.

notes: Design: the central service is a coord serve (POST /v1/run with {argv}, bearer token per operator, one key file each, group scopes, plain-http refusal beyond loopback: kb/_self/coordination.md), so a thin client needs no new network surface: submit, follow and status are coord operations on job/ID keys. Scope set by the operator's answer to gate g1 (2026-11-08): central executors, a server kbjob.py serve and GitLab CI jobs, may run every operation, landings and worker sessions included, wherever the job's placement puts it. This story is the queue and the executor kinds only; the placement decision (OPA policy, overrides, CODEOWNERS), identities, worker branches on the integration remote, the server's clones, CI triggering, cost caps and records are the stories of EP-p4guu2ip, so a job record here carries a placement that defaults to the workstation. Authority: a workstation executor runs a job only when the job's operator equals the operator of its own key file and its host is its own; the operation table stays closed (ST-nwwcf3kk); no job answers a gate. Complement stance: no Agent Mail or Beads piece does this (kb public/agents/coordination-tools.md:54), so nothing is rebuilt; coord serve is what is extended. Related: EP-fxrzbuza only where it also extends coord serve.
